length.text: About 90 to 122 cm; up to about 1.5-1.8 m

overview.text: The Black Kingsnake is a non-venomous kingsnake of the south-eastern United States. Like other kingsnakes it is a strong constrictor.

identification.text: Black, with widely spaced small yellow or cream speckles that are bigger and more numerous along the sides.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually about 90 to 122 cm long; some reach 147 to 183 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The south-eastern USA from southern Illinois and Ohio south along the Appalachian foothills to Alabama and Mississippi.

habitat.text: Many habitats - old farms, debris piles, floodplain edges and thick brush by streams and swamps. In some states it is one of the snakes people meet most often.

recognise.text: Shiny black with small pale speckles.
